vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: sql-generator
Version: 2.3.6

The skill bundle is a legitimate SQL generation utility that uses bash scripts (sql.sh and script.sh) to provide SQL templates, indexing advice, and mock data generation. The logic is entirely local, relying on hardcoded templates and basic keyword matching to output text, with no evidence of network activity, data exfiltration, or malicious prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill is internally consistent with a local SQL generation toolkit: included bash scripts generate SQL and write small data/log files under the user's data directory, and it does not request credentials or perform network activity.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (SQL generator, DDL, explain, mock data, migrate) aligns with the included scripts (sql.sh generates CREATE/DDL, examples for common tables). Minor mismatch: SKILL.md lists commands like optimize/create/mock/cheatsheet while the shipped scripts expose overlapping but not identical command names (sql.sh: table, query, join, index, migrate, seed, explain; script.sh: query/import/export/transform/...). This is plausible but worth noting.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime behavior stays within expected scope (generating SQL text). The provided scripts write files to a data directory ($XDG_DATA_HOME or $HOME/.local/share/sql-generator) and append to history.log/data.log; SKILL.md does not explicitly warn about creating those files. No access to system credentials, no network calls, and no reading of unrelated system config.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with bundled shell scripts and no install spec; nothing is downloaded or installed from external sources.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables, no credentials, and does not reference external service tokens. Its filesystem writes are limited to a user-scoped data directory (configurable via SQL_GENERATOR_DIR/XDG_DATA_HOME).
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Does not request permanent/always presence. The scripts create and use their own data directory and logs but do not modify other skills or system-wide agent settings. Autonomous invocation is enabled (default) — normal for skills.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be a local SQL-generation toolkit implemented in bash. Before installing, be aware it will create and write files under $XDG_DATA_HOME/sql-generator or ~/.local/share/sql-generator (data.log, history.log). There are no network calls or credential requests detected, but the SKILL.md command list and shipped scripts' commands do not perfectly match — review the included scripts if you need specific functionality. If you are uncomfortable with a tool writing files to your home directory, either set SQL_GENERATOR_DIR to a location you control or don't install the skill.
